api_deviations_from_brief: render_callback / capture_callback take no separate &Counters: the ring ends embed the shared Arc<Counters> so a mismatched counter set is impossible; counters are reachable via Consumer::counters/Producer::counters
Provider methods take grant: Option<&DeviceGrant> (brief: &DeviceGrant) because the brief requires 'missing grant => Unauthorized'; enumerate also needs a grant (no ambient device access)

Added beyond brief: PushError::DeviceLost, Counters underrun_frames + dropped_frames, CloseReport residual_frames/device_lost/callbacks/loopback_samples/reconciles()/is_clean(), Limits.max_open_streams admission, DeviceError::AdmissionDenied, ring_blocks >= 2

Full refusal on the output ring counts one overrun + one discontinuity per the brief test, but dropped_frames stays 0 (the caller keeps the block); a healthy backpressured stream therefore shows overruns > 0 with Outcome Success (native smoke above: overruns=30 from retried Full offers). Real loss = dropped_frames > 0 or device_lost.
cpal stream runs on an owner thread this crate spawns instead of being held by the handle (Stream Send-ness differs per platform); readiness handshake over a bounded channel with 15 s open wait
limitations: Sample format is interleaved f32 only; no resampling, conversion, MIDI, record-to-file (brief non-goals). Native open of a device whose shared-mode format differs from the request is refused (Unavailable), never converted.
cpal backend is output only; open_input returns Unavailable. Native device loss and native underrun/overrun accounting beyond the one smoke run are untested (no way to inject loss on a real device).
If a native build_output_stream never returns, CpalBackend::drop joins the owner thread and can block (cpal's 5 s build timeout bounds the normal case).
Software input device ramp is exact only for the first 2^24 samples (f32).
Windows timer granularity makes the software cadence coarse; the schedule catches up rather than drifts; jitter is not asserted.
